Found by the whole-branch review gating the v6.116.0 release. Low severity — pure name drift in historical audit-trail documents, no functional impact.

A future maintainer greps for `checkPostTeardownPin` (per these permanently-committed documents' own text) to find or modify the post-teardown handler, gets zero hits in any `.js` source, and wrongly concludes the feature was never shipped or was silently removed.

groups.body:
## Current State

Wiring `checkPostTeardownReanchor` into `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` for `ExitWorktree`/`git worktree remove` (landed via #703's continuation, commit range `42a8bbb05..afd33e3e9`) means `post-tool-use.js` now receives `ExitWorktree` events for the first time. This activates `stampAdHocRunDir`'s non-EnterWorktree branch (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js:445`) against an input shape it was never exercised against: it calls `resolveWorktreePathViaPorcelain(ctx)`, which shells out `git -C <cwd> worktree list --porcelain` against the just-deleted worktree directory — guaranteed to fail — but unconditionally writes `ADHOC_WORKTREE_CHECKED_MARKER` regardless of that outcome.

Found by the whole-branch review gating the v6.116.0 release (CLAUDE.md's Releasing section) — confirmed, not yet fixed. Narrow/edge-case severity: requires an ad-hoc (non-pipeline) session that later creates a different worktree via a raw `git worktree add` (bypassing `EnterWorktree`) within the same session.

## Deliverables

- Guard the marker write in `stampAdHocRunDir`'s non-EnterWorktree branch so it is only written on a successful resolution (or otherwise distinguishes "checked and found nothing" from "the lookup itself couldn't run because the target no longer exists").
- Add a regression test: an `ExitWorktree(action:'remove')` event must not permanently defeat the #1333 ad-hoc-stamping mechanism for a later raw `git worktree add` in the same session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An `ExitWorktree(action:'remove')` PostToolUse event does not write `ADHOC_WORKTREE_CHECKED_MARKER` when the porcelain lookup fails because the target directory is already gone.
- A session that runs `ExitWorktree(remove)` and later creates a worktree via raw `git worktree add` still gets that worktree stamped by `stampAdHocRunDir`.

## Failure scenario this fixes

An ad-hoc (non-pipeline) session runs `ExitWorktree(action:'remove')`. `stampAdHocRunDir` calls `resolveWorktreePathViaPorcelain(ctx)` against the now-deleted directory; it fails, but the marker file is still written. If that same session later creates a different worktree via a raw `git worktree add` (bypassing `EnterWorktree`), `stampAdHocRunDir`'s non-EnterWorktree path is now permanently skipped for the rest of the session (marker already exists) — no run-dir is ever stamped for that later worktree, silently defeating the #1333 mechanism this branch exists for.

Origin: capture

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:sweep`'s `## Next Actions` block (`plugin/skills/sweep/SKILL.md`) renders in a
fixed order: the top `/claude-tweaks:backlog attention` pick (when present, replacing the
`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` slot per the precedence rule) -> `/claude-tweaks:dispatch {grants}` ->
`/claude-tweaks:tidy --approve` -> `/claude-tweaks:backlog attention`.

Observed live on a real sweep run: tidy staged only two trivial, already-vetted items (one
`docs/REGISTRY.md` line addition, three stale `bot:in-progress` label removals on issues whose
claims were already stale/released) -- yet `tidy --approve` rendered third in the Next Actions
block, after a `backlog refine #N` re-authorization pick and a `dispatch` call that kicks off
new autonomous builds. The user flagged this live as counter-intuitive: closing out a fully
vetted, zero-judgment batch should be the cheapest, fastest thing to clear -- not buried behind
two heavier, judgment-requiring actions.

## Deliverables

- Re-examine `sweep/SKILL.md`'s `## Next Actions` fixed ordering (`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` /
  `/claude-tweaks:tidy --approve` / `/claude-tweaks:backlog attention`, with the needs-you
  precedence rule only ever replacing the `/dispatch` slot) and decide whether "apply
  already-staged, mechanically-vetted proposals" should sort ahead of "start new autonomous
  work" or "resolve a re-authorization."
- Either (a) reorder so `tidy --approve` leads whenever this run's tidy step staged anything,
  with dispatch/refine picks following, or (b) if the current order is intentional, add one
  line to `sweep/SKILL.md` stating the rationale so a future reader isn't left guessing.
- Check whether the same ordering question applies to `tidy/SKILL.md`'s own Next Actions
  derivation rule (the "Approve ({N})" line's position relative to a Yours group's batch line)
  for consistency across both skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sweep/SKILL.md`'s `## Next Actions` section either reorders `tidy --approve` ahead of
  `dispatch`/the needs-you pick whenever tidy staged anything this run, or documents why the
  current order is deliberate.
- No change to the underlying tidy/refine/dispatch mechanics -- this is purely about the
  recommended ordering of paste-ready lines in the close-out render.

Surface: backend

## Current State

Record #649 added `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s fan-out single-assistant-message-rule
sentence and per-site citations (AC1, fully test-pinned in `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`,
18/18 passing). AC2 — "A `/specify` red-team over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues launches its
personas in ≤ (number of sub-issues) assistant messages, verified in the transcript by `Agent`
tool_use blocks sharing a message id" — is a live-behavior criterion that cannot be verified by a
static `node --test` assertion; it can only be confirmed by observing an actual future `/specify`
decomposition run's transcript.

## Deliverables

Confirm, at the next `/specify` decomposition run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues, that
persona dispatch actually batches into ≤N assistant messages per `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s
fan-out single-assistant-message rule and `red-team.md`'s per-sub-issue batching unit. Record the
observation (transcript excerpt or note) against this item, or file a defect against
`red-team.md`'s dispatch prose if it does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

A `/specify` run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues is observed; its persona `Agent` tool_use
calls are confirmed (via transcript `tool_use` block message-id grouping) to arrive in ≤ (number of
sub-issues) assistant messages.

## Technical Approach

Wait for (or trigger) a `/claude-tweaks:specify` decomposition-mode run that produces 2 or more
`ceremony:standard` sub-issue records — `ceremony-check` (`assess-agent-autonomy/ceremony-check.md`)
resolves the tier per sub-issue during that run's own Step 3, so the tier isn't knowable until the
run happens. Once such a run occurs, inspect that session's stored transcript for the Step 5
red-team dispatch (`specify/red-team.md`'s Parallel dispatch section): locate the `Agent` tool_use
blocks for each dispatched persona and group them by the assistant message id each block belongs
to. Confirm the number of distinct assistant message ids covering all persona dispatches for a
given sub-issue is ≤ the number of sub-issues in that batch. Use the same read-only transcript
inspection method `transcript-payload-verification` documents for reading this session's own
locally-stored transcript, rather than instrumenting or modifying `red-team.md` itself.

If the count exceeds the bound, file a defect issue against `red-team.md`'s dispatch prose
(quoting the transcript grouping that violates the rule) instead of editing the file directly from
this record — this record's own deliverable is the observation, not the fix.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/specify/red-team.md` — the per-sub-issue persona dispatch procedure being observed
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — the fan-out single-assistant-message rule this observation verifies compliance with
- `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — AC1's existing static test coverage (unaffected by this record)

## Gotchas

- This record's acceptance criterion depends on an external event (a live `/specify` decomposition
  run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues happening) that this record cannot itself trigger on a
  fixed schedule — it may sit open for some time until a qualifying run occurs naturally, or until
  someone deliberately runs one to close it out.
- A qualifying run must be observed via its own transcript at the time it happens; this record
  cannot be resolved from historical data if no already-completed run's transcript is still
  available.

## Original request

Verify /specify red-team fan-out batching at next live multi-sub-issue run (#649 AC2)
